channel.title: The Wire · compute.world
channel.description: Sovereign AI and compute infrastructure signals, scored for credibility. From The Compute Net Worth Index.

item.title: NVIDIA and six Wall Street giants form platforms to mobilize $500B+ for AI infrastructure
item.description: NVIDIA partners with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to establish independent compute-financing platforms targeting over $500 billion of third-party capital, with NVIDIA guaranteeing up to 25 percent of chip residual value on individual deals. The capital constraint on the global buildout just grew a dedicated channel, and GPUs were declared an investable asset class. [Signal 95, Confirmed, via NVIDIA IR] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Firebird's Armenia AI factory goes live: frontier-market sovereign compute has a working example
item.description: The Hrazdan facility went from site to operation in about six months on NVIDIA and Dell infrastructure, with a roadmap of 70,000+ GPUs and 300 MW by end-2027 and NVIDIA stating intent to invest. The proof of concept for small-state compute conversion. [Signal 92, Confirmed, via NVIDIA blog] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Indonesia's Indosat launches Zankore, a 1 GW AI-factory platform with Ooredoo, NVIDIA and Nokia
item.description: First 200 MW of GB300-class capacity targeted for H1 2027 at Batang, Central Java, with Qatari capital leading. Southeast Asia's largest sovereign-flavored compute commitment to date. [Signal 78, Corroborated, via Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: EU opens the AI Gigafactories call: up to 7 sites, €10B public money, bids due November
item.description: EuroHPC launches the formal tender for gigafactory sites across at least seven member states, targeting over €30 billion total investment with selection in early 2027. Europe's answer arrives as a procurement document. [Signal 90, Confirmed, via EuroHPC (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: South Korea's AIDC Alliance sets an 18.4 GW datacenter target by 2035
item.description: Following the 260,000-GPU national program announced at APEC, the alliance formalizes the most aggressive national capacity target published anywhere, with UAE export ambitions attached. [Signal 66, Corroborated, via TechTimes] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Nepal books record power exports: NPR 29.32B for 3.877 TWh at roughly $0.054 per kWh
item.description: Export earnings rose 68 percent year on year. The same electrons routed through contracted GPU cloud would gross roughly 20 to 40 times more, which is the entire compute-conversion argument in one fiscal year. [Signal 68, Corroborated, via Republica (NEA data)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: The UAE gets a named lane in US export law, with an April 2027 sting attached
item.description: Federal Register rule 91 FR 43034 moves the UAE to Country Group A:5 and names approved entities, while G42 and Core42's license-free status expires April 6, 2027 unless they become US companies. The template for compute diplomacy, and its price, in one document. [Signal 94, Confirmed, via US Federal Register] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Kazakhstan signs $10B with NVIDIA and Firebird for a gigawatt-scale Data Center Valley at Ekibastuz
item.description: 300 MW rising toward 1 GW and 100,000 GPUs on coal-basin power, with a stated $3 billion per year export ambition. In its officials' words: transforming Ekibastuz coal into digital export revenue. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via Times of Central Asia] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Meta signs its first India AI datacenter deal: a 168 MW JV inside Reliance's Jamnagar campus
item.description: Part of Reliance's stated $110 billion AI plan, with 120+ MW already live in H2 2026. The largest private-sector compute bet in the Global South acquires an anchor tenant. [Signal 80, Corroborated, via TechCrunch] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Huang at GTC Taipei: AI factories at $50-60B per GW now, $80-100B per GW soon
item.description: The clearest 2026 restatement of the price of compute capacity, and the basis for this index's ceiling band. Every token is revenue, per Huang; every watt is now priced accordingly. [Signal 76, Corroborated, via SiliconANGLE] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: GAO rules the US chip-export non-enforcement posture procedurally defective
item.description: Decision B-337935 holds that the May 2025 non-enforcement announcement was itself a rule that was never submitted to Congress. The legal floor under most emerging markets' GPU access is officially contested. [Signal 93, Confirmed, via US GAO (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Microsoft and G42's Kenya campus stalls for lack of power
item.description: Chips were available; electricity was not. The clearest single data point that energy, not silicon, is the binding constraint on the global buildout. [Signal 75, Corroborated, via Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Stargate UK pauses over energy costs
item.description: The flagship western sovereign deal, 31,000 GPUs planned, halts on power prices while the North East AI Growth Zone still advertises 1.1 GW. Readiness without affordable electrons has a ceiling of its own. [Signal 70, Corroborated, via Data Centre Magazine] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Microsoft contracts 30,000 Rubin GPUs at Nscale's hydro-powered Narvik site
item.description: Stargate Norway's capacity finds a hyperscale offtaker above the Arctic Circle. Cold, cheap, firm power keeps winning the contracts that latency arguments said it could not. [Signal 78, Corroborated, via Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Brazil approves a 5 GW grid connection for Scala's AI City
item.description: Eldorado do Sul's campus gets state sign-off for up to 4.75 GW of planned capacity, roughly $50 billion, with phase one operational. Latin America's largest compute project is now also its most grid-real. [Signal 74, Corroborated, via Data Centre Magazine] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: ByteDance begins construction on a ~$39B campus at Pecém with a 20-year wind PPA
item.description: 300 MW first phase toward roughly 1 GW in Ceará, wind-fired and export-oriented. The largest Chinese AI-infrastructure project abroad is rising in Brazil. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: S&P lifts Paraguay to investment grade, joining Moody's
item.description: BBB- lands on the country holding the index's largest redirectable power surplus relative to size, roughly 40 TWh a year currently exported at commodity prices. Capital access arrives before the compute does. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via Bloomberg] More: https://compute.world/wire.html
